### 2026-10-07 – #Day 2: Starting on the PCB

**3h**

#Day 2: Starting on the PCB

Today, I started work on the PCB and began to flesh out how I want to make this project personal to me. First was finishing up the schematic, which didn't take long.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 210532](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/5131f1f188839076061b4f9b3ea7af7829de9639a87c10e66d0d3560b12e80e8.png)

Afterwards, I then had to import the schematic into the PCB editor. However, when I tried to import it, I realized that I didn't have a footprint for the XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD, and the only one that showed was for the C6-DIP model instead. After a LOAD of trouble with assigning footprints to components and a beg to the ChatGPT overlords, I had finally imported the ESP-32 into the PCB editor.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 212422](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/3c9263515c018fe6fb118c292ccb7551e9d8acde49aeedf6e9b150e0a86d7a7f.png)

My troubles still weren't over yet, as then I slowly realized that every part had the wrong footprint, and that I had to restart work on the PCB, which SUCKED because I began prototyping the designs at this phase.

After a quick visit through all 7 stages of grief, I re-added the schematic with the CORRECT FOOTPRINTS this time, and  then started thinking about how I want to make this project unique. My current idea is to make the PCB in the shape of a floppy disk, and replace the cutesy face with Doomguy or some other retro video game (If you're reading this, Hack Club, I see what you did there with naming this competition "Half-Life"!).  Another idea, because I thought that a floppy disk wouldn't be too recognizable, would be to put the circuitry, like the ESP 32, resistors, motion sensors, etc. in a mini classic PC case, and the OLED in a faux CRT display, then the keys would go onto a tiny keyboard just outside. Both would be a nice homage to retro gaming.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 233319](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9cba91ea380688ea5beff7820db531b8b16dd1d89a3756613ffd35596a06577d.png)

### 2026-10-08 – *Day 3 - Finishing my first PCB*

**3h**

*Day 3 - Finishing my first PCB*
Today I finished routing the PCB and the main PCB design. I'm going to stick with the floppy disk design for now, but might make it bigger if I need to.

LOTS of time was spent routing the PCB, as I had to make sure I didn't "box" the ESP-32 with trace connections, and avoid the text, as the ink used to make it is non-conductive, and otherwise would result in a short. It was VERY annoying and I had to change component layouts to make the tracing actually work, but after a good bit of blood, sweat, and tears it was done. I used the Design Rules Checker to make sure what I did was actually valid. I also created a ground pour layer.

Routing the PCB:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 205136](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/55e3fd38a9e427d21bfc73634b981344c8c1fcb219158e427e34f1f606f36c69.png)

After that, I wanted to decorate my PCB, as it only felt right to make this board truly mine. I searched up a tutorial on Youtube (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DZ0T5gWkHgs) researching on how to import images onto my board. I tried to import a face of Doomguy grinning, but that turned out VERY messy on the PCB and I didn't bother. Instead, I put a lambda logo for Half-Life, since, you know... (Wow, this is the third unfunny Half-Life joke I made the whole competition!) Anyway, I slapped it onto the board and it looked great.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 234834](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/7e68168a1348e47855d77992d87e7e6018c8e9889edb0f01e3f0df3bc43b0f8d.png)

Finally, I began to think about additional features to expand onto this project. I'm thinking about adding a rechargable battery onto it to make it portable, and a joystick for more interaction. I want to create a parts list when I finally decide all of the hardware and software features that I want for this project. Some parts I already have at home, but others I will need to buy. For now, I just finished the base Starbie features.

The PCB so far:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 222519](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/7998c2ce9411a6e172724b1b790fa2c0602dc2d90a32a6da15d29a0fb9dc2b72.png)

### 2026-10-09 – *Day 4: Some New Additions*

**3h**

*Day 4: Some New Additions*

Today, I added the features from my previous journal, which were a joystick and a rechargable battery. I first started with adding them to the schematics, which wasn't hard. I just had to wire up some changes and additions to the PCB. I felt uneasy, as I had never added a battery to a project before.

The completed schematics:
![Screenshot 2026-10-08 215606](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/8c75b9a87173fbd8b9d6bff7f38c732d7eb13be6de7afeeb0c68569f891aa4ce.png)

The next part was the PCB, and this was arguably the worst part of this project. First of all, the default footprint for this project didn't have the bottom battery pads that are normally there, which then, I decided to download an identical footprint, save for the fact that it has the battery pads. After getting everything wired back up in the schematics editor, I began to realize that I couldn't wire to the battery pads for some reason. I investigated the actual component, and after a long bit of troubleshooting, i created a little bit of excess "wire", and then went through the pads. That seemed to work, for now at least. Onto the PCB editor, I tried to wire to the terminals, but something was blocking it. This troubled me for a long time and I begged and pleaded with ChatGPT for an answer, and after a long struggle, opening the footprint editor revealed some kind of zone blocking traces from getting through. One checkmark later, I could now route traces there. I finished wiring the battery terminals and the joystick and oh, I had done it. The main hardware was finally over.

Me trying to figure out why traces don't connect to the battery terminal:

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 224324](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/e5d1b2195007fdde3e644e6dbae9d175f3311983bbaaec17660c3630a16b4d97.png)

Granted, I will make some final changes to the board, like flipping the ESP-32 180 degrees so that the port faces outward instead of towards the board, or a voltage regulator so I don't fry my ESP-32, but after this point is just software and writing out the BOM. The joystick will provide interactibility, while the charging port has portability. I might add a battery percentage or some small games you can play with your "pet". For now, this is what I have.

Close-to-the-end PCB:

![Screenshot 2026-10-08 225933](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/c6d49ed6bca1885b9a18b2f8dc6ac2948768cce78e01cb6b8bb445c1aed22a8d.png)

### 2026-10-10 – # Day 5: Finalizing the PCB

**3h**

# Day 5: Finalizing the PCB

Today I finished the PCB and the BOM, on the github repository.
This journal is going to be a bit of a short one, but it that's because it was mostly just finalization instead of large changes.

First, I flipped the ESP32 around so you can actually charge it, and routed it accordingly, which was surprisingly, more difficult than I thought. After routing I created the ground pour again, as I have to, and then it was complete.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 005348](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/0be9c5bbd1c45f1c3bc028365b4fd58acd553e2fad4e36e284449f503718b61d.png)

I then went back and finished the Github repo, adding a README with an image, the BOM, and completed PCB. The BOM still needs to account for prices, along with the battery, joystick, and other things I need to add, but I can make it work.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 220721](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/47400c75a3029e7208f6b77e13032b485482a4705442a9173c3cf068e5224d1b.png)

Lastly, I finished up the footprints, giving the battery a JST connector and the joystick a 5-pin female pin header. From here is just getting ready for the final day and software. Once again, I'm thinking using EVA from Command and Conquer or Doomguy, as they are iconic in 90's gaming in my opinion, and represent 2 of some of my favorite games.
